title.en: Molecules: a Lecture to the British Association
title.zh: 分子：在英国科学促进会的讲演

author.zh: 詹姆斯·克拉克·麦克斯韦

year_display.zh: 1873 年 9 月在布拉德福德的讲演

edition.en: As printed under the title The Theory of Molecules in The Popular Science Monthly, vol. 4 (January 1874), and transcribed on English Wikisource. The lecture complete; the two tables of molecular data printed after it are omitted, and the six lines Maxwell quotes from Tennyson are run together with slashes.
edition.zh: 据《大众科学月刊》第 4 卷（1874 年 1 月）以“分子的理论”为题刊印的文本，以英文维基文库转录本为底本。讲演全文；文后所附两张分子数据表从略，麦克斯韦所引丁尼生的六行诗以斜线连排。

basis.en: Delivered in 1873 and printed in 1873–74; the author died in 1879. The lines quoted from Tennyson’s Lucretius were published in 1868; Tennyson died in 1892.
basis.zh: 1873 年讲演，1873–74 年刊印；作者卒于 1879 年。所引丁尼生《卢克莱修》诗句发表于 1868 年，丁尼生卒于 1892 年。

note.en: Maxwell explains to a general audience how one can know the size, speed and number of things no one has ever seen, from Democritus and Lucretius through diffusion and the kinetic theory of gases. The close is the part people remember: a hydrogen molecule vibrates at the same rate in Sirius as on earth, so every molecule carries a standard of measure as distinct as the metre kept in Paris. His final inference, that identical molecules must have been made by no natural process, did not survive later physics, which found natural processes that make atoms, in the early universe and in stars, and explained why every one of a kind is identical; the picture of standards that do not wear still holds.
note.zh: 麦克斯韦向普通听众讲解，人怎样才能知道从没有人见过的东西的大小、速度和数目：从德谟克利特和卢克莱修讲起，一直讲到扩散和气体分子运动论。人们记住的是结尾：一个氢分子在天狼星上和在地球上以同样的频率振动，所以每个分子都带着一种与巴黎的米原器同样清晰的度量标准。他最后的推论——完全相同的分子不可能由任何自然过程造成——已被后来的物理学推翻：人们找到了在宇宙早期和恒星内部造出原子的自然过程，也解释了为什么同一种类的每一个都完全相同；但那幅“标准永不磨损”的图景依然成立。

excerpt.orig: the molecules out of which these systems are built—the foundation-stones of the material universe—remain unbroken and unworn.
excerpt.en: the molecules out of which these systems are built—the foundation-stones of the material universe—remain unbroken and unworn.
excerpt.zh: 构成这些体系的分子——物质宇宙的基石——却始终完好无损，从不磨蚀。

gloss.en: Greek, “having like parts”: the name given, by Aristotle and later Lucretius, to Anaxagoras’s view that each kind of stuff is made of parts like the whole.
gloss.zh: 希腊语，意为“由相似的部分组成”。亚里士多德和后来的卢克莱修用这个词来称呼阿那克萨哥拉的学说：每一种物质都由与整体相似的部分构成。

gloss.en: Samuel Johnson’s Dictionary of the English Language, 1755.
gloss.zh: 塞缪尔·约翰逊的《英语词典》，1755 年出版。

gloss.en: About 460 metres a second, faster than sound travels in air (about 340).
gloss.zh: 约合每秒 460 米，比声音在空气中传播的速度（约每秒 340 米）还快。

gloss.en: The British Association’s section for economic science and statistics.
gloss.zh: 不列颠科学促进会下设的经济科学与统计组。

gloss.en: That is 1.9 × 10¹⁹. The modern value, Loschmidt’s number, is about 2.69 × 10¹⁹ per cubic centimetre, so this “third rank” estimate was of the right size.
gloss.zh: 即 1.9×10¹⁹。今天的数值（洛施密特常数）约为每立方厘米 2.69×10¹⁹ 个，可见这个“第三等”的估计在数量级上是对的。

gloss.at: the metre of the Archives of Paris
gloss.en: The platinum bar made in 1799 and kept in the Archives nationales as the standard of the metre, until the international prototype of 1889.
gloss.zh: 1799 年制成、保存在巴黎国家档案馆的铂质米尺，是当时的米标准，直到 1889 年才被国际米原器取代。

note.en: A great physicist explaining invisible things to a general audience with real clarity; the ending’s argument from identical molecules to a maker has not survived later physics.
note.zh: 伟大物理学家向大众清楚讲解看不见的东西；结尾由分子全同推出造物者的论证，未能经受后来物理学的检验。
